deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page continues the previous folio. Two lenses are fixed: a crown lens (log n = 0.1804591, n ≈ 1.515; its radii r, r' are 'wie vorhin') and a flint lens (mean colour log n = 0.2046002, n ≈ 1.6018) whose surfaces are numbered here as 3 and 4. The flint has axial thickness 0.8. Gauss is designing a two-lens achromatic telescope objective, in the spirit of his 1817 'achromatische Doppelobjective'. He treats the third radius r'' as the free parameter and tries several 'hypotheses' for it. For each trial, r''' (the fourth radius) is fixed by an achromatism condition. A marginal ray is then traced exactly, and its focus is compared with the paraxial focus of the mean colour. The 'Error' is the longitudinal spherical aberration in units of 1e-4. The previous page gave Hyp. I: marginal 281.6927 against paraxial 281.5481, error +1446.

A. PARAXIAL PART, HYPOTHESIS 2 (r'' = 10^1.6782472 = 47.67022).
(1) For three colours i = 1, 2, 3 the flint indices are n1 ≈ 1.5818 (log 0.1991543), n2 = 1.60177 (log 0.2046002) and n3 ≈ 1.6217 (log 0.2099785). The page tabulates log K_i = 0.4343731, 0.4251697, 0.4163767, where K_i = n_i/(n_i - 1); I checked this for colour 2.
(2) c_i = 0.017286504, 0.017079173, 0.016885432. My reading: c_i = 1/((n_i - 1) s_i), where s_i is the colour-dependent paraxial convergence distance coming out of the crown lens.
(3) 1/r'' = 0.020977454.
(4) Surface 3, air to flint: n/s'' = 1/s + (n - 1)/r'', rewritten as s'' = K/(c + 1/r''). The logs 8.5827899, 8.5804302, 8.5782137 are log(c_i + 1/r''), giving s''_i = 71.05313, 69.94224, 68.89108.
(5) Subtract the thickness 0.8: distances from surface 4 are 70.25313, 69.14224, 68.09108 (logs 1.8466657, 1.8397434, 1.8330896).
(6) Achromatism condition. Surface 4 (flint to air) gives 1/s''' = n/s - (n - 1)/r'''. Requiring s''' to be equal for colours 1 and 3 gives
 r''' = (n3 - n1)/(n3/s3 - n1/s1).
 Numerically: n1/s1 = 0.02251586, n3/s3 = 0.02381707, difference log 7.1143474, log(n3 - n1) = 8.6011905. Hence log r''' = 1.4868431, i.e. r''' = 30.67913.
(7) Focal distances. Using s''' = (1/(n - 1))/(K/s - 1/r'''), with K/s = 0.03869968, 0.03849695, 0.03830773 and log 1/(n - 1) = 0.2352188, 0.2205695, 0.2063982:
 s'''_1 = 281.5705, s'''_2 = 281.5830, s'''_3 = 281.5710.
 Colours 1 and 3 are united; colour 2 shows a secondary spectrum of about 0.012.
 An earlier column (278.15, 278.05, 277.92) belongs to an earlier, unclear trial.

B. EXACT MARGINAL RAY, HYPOTHESIS 2. Input from the previous page: the ray crosses the axis at a'' = 95.300277 behind surface 3, at slope u = 5°50'26.613".
(1) Surface 3: sin φ = (a - r'') sin u / r''. In logs: 1.6778811 + 9.0075917 + 8.3217528 gives 9.0072256, so φ = 5°50'8.170".
(2) sin φ' = sin φ / n: 8.8026254, so φ' = 3°38'22.151".
(3) u' = u + φ - φ' = 8°2'12.632".
(4) a' - r'' = r'' sin φ'/sin u' = 21.64387. Then a' = 69.31409; less the thickness, 68.51409.
(5) Surface 4: sin φ = (68.51409 - 30.67913) sin u'/r''', with log 9.2365878, so φ = 9°55'42.802". Then sin φ' = n sin φ gives φ' = 16°1'55.877".
(6) u'' = u' - (φ' - φ) = 1°55'59.557".
(7) r''' sin φ'/sin u'' = 251.16790; adding r''' gives 281.84703.
(8) Error II = 281.84703 - 281.5830 = +0.2640.

C. HYPOTHESIS 3 (r'' = 10^1.6804583 = 47.913544).
(1) Paraxial: 1/r'' = 0.020870923. Then s'' = 71.25149, 70.13855, 69.08545, and after the thickness 70.45149, 69.33855, 68.28545.
(2) K/s = 0.03859072, 0.03838795, 0.03819869.
(3) New r''': 1/r''' = 0.03248507 (log 8.5116838), so r''' = 30.78338.
(4) Foci: logs of the differences 7.7857319, 7.7710639, 7.7569113 give 281.5055, 281.5177, 281.5055.
(5) Marginal ray: φ = 5°46'34.630", φ' = 3°36'8.842", u' = 8°0'52.401", a' - r'' = 21.592781, a' = 69.506325, then 68.706325.
(6) Surface 4: φ = 9°53'24.883", φ' = 15°58'9.473", u'' = 1°56'7.811". Back focal distance 250.75713 + 30.78338 = 281.54051.
(7) Error III = 281.54051 - 281.5177 = +0.0228.

D. SUMMARY AND SCRATCH. The summary reads I +1446, II +2640, III +228, IV +21. 'Hyp IV' is evidently an interpolated r'' (regula falsi on log r'') that drives the marginal error almost to zero. The scratch figures (984 + 7.1, 416 + 7.6, 1194, 12111, 2280 ...) are such interpolation arithmetic.
errors: No substantive computational errors were found. Every check I made (sums of logarithms, angle bookkeeping u' = u + φ - φ' and u'' = u' - (φ' - φ), distances, focal lengths, error differences) is consistent to the last place within 7-place table accuracy.
Hyp 2, third colour: log s3 was first written 1.8370902 and struck out. The value actually used for n3/s3 = 0.02381707 is log 68.09108 = 1.83309, so the slip was corrected.

Hyp 3: the colour-2 value s'' was at first miswritten (begins with 79 or 70, bold correction) and fixed to 70.13855. Gauss also corrected several of the logs 7.785..., 7.756... by striking them through.
Colours 1 and 3 do not come out exactly equal (281.5705 against 281.5710 in Hyp 2). This is a rounding residue of r''' and is harmless.

Interpretive caveat: the dispersion implied for the three colours (Δn ≈ ±0.02 about 1.602) is large. These may be extreme spectral colours or conventional trial values; my identification of the logs as n and n/(n-1) is numerically secure but the physical colours are not stated.

results.what: Paraxial refraction in the form s' = K/(c + 1/r), with K = n/(n-1), and s''' = (1/(n-1))/(K/s - 1/r), applied colour by colour through a two-lens objective.
results.modern_name: Paraxial (first-order) ray trace / refraction invariant at a single spherical surface
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-19th century dioptrics (Euler, Lagrange, Gauss's Dioptrische Untersuchungen 1841)

results.what: Choosing the last radius by r''' = (n3 - n1)/(n3/s3 - n1/s1) so that two colours have a common focus; the residual of the middle colour is about 0.012.
results.modern_name: Achromatization condition for a doublet (two-colour correction), secondary spectrum
results.usually_credited_to: Dollond/Hall (achromat), Clairaut, d'Alembert, Euler; Gauss 1817 for his objective

results.what: Exact trigonometric tracing of a marginal ray via sin φ = (a - r) sin u / r, sin φ' = sin φ/n, u' = u + φ - φ', a' - r = r sin φ'/sin u'.
results.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler era onward); later systematized by Seidel, Steinheil, and the Zeiss optical workers

results.what: Iterating the radius r'' (Hypotheses I-IV, with interpolation) to make the marginal focus coincide with the paraxial focus while keeping two colours united.
results.modern_name: Correction of longitudinal spherical aberration together with achromatism; design of the Gauss two-meniscus objective
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss (1817, 'Über die achromatischen Doppelobjective')

deep.surprise_reason: This is numerical design work (paraxial trace, achromatism condition, exact marginal-ray trace, trial-and-interpolate on a radius) for an achromatic doublet objective. That is exactly the program of Gauss's published 1817 objective paper and his known dioptric studies. The methods are standard for the period; the page is valuable only as a record of his working procedure.
